# RETRO: PR #12264 (team 4)

## What worked
- A small, well-scoped brief. Both reviewers converged independently on the same core conclusions from different coreutils versions (9.7 source vs 9.12/9.11 source plus runtime).
- A neutral cross-examination follow-up turned the single-sourced `mkdir` claim into an independently confirmed one within minutes.
- Checking base drift before briefing (script unchanged between PR base and quattro tip) removed a whole class of applicability questions.

## Process deviations (recorded)
- Opus reviewer: several reads exceeded the 50-line content bound (three parallel `pr.diff` reads of about 138 lines total; grep listings of 51-78 lines; one 57-line read; one `cut -c1-220` re-display of already fully read menu lines). The reviewer reports that no policy text was truncated and that no evidence depended on a projection. This is a storage and read-hygiene deviation only.
- Opus reviewer: `review-v1` plan initialized but never run (superseded by v2). Preserved.
- Sol reviewer: one host-side `grep -E` filename-selection listing ran outside review.py. It was a listing only, not a probe, and no result from it is credited.
- Sol follow-up: ran its Git history queries via review.py on a private `git clone --mirror --no-local` of `src/mirror`. Reading the mirror was host-side and non-mutating (the clone destination was its own output).
- Coordinator: first reads of this workflow were 50-line chunks as required. The team-4.json registry was summarized through a python projection rather than read in full. It is a state file, not policy.

## Improvements
- The brief's 50-line rule is easy to break with grep listings. Suggest that reviewers pipe listings through `wc -l` first, or page with `sed -n`.
- The Sol reviewer cited line 1188 for a line at 1189 (link range still correct). The coordinator checked line numbers against pinned source before publishing them.

## Tool notes
- No Omadev use. No tool bugs found.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** both changes do what the PR describes. No behavior defect was found in the inspected and tested scope. One small cleanup and one optional test case are noted below.

### Launcher entry now written only after a successful start

**Verified:** `windows-vm.desktop` is the marker the Omarchy menu reads to disable Install and show Remove. It is now written only after `priv up` (the `docker compose up -d` step) succeeds, so every earlier exit leaves the menu offering Install.

```text
install_windows            base                      head
-------------------------  ------------------------  ------------------------
after omarchy-pkg-add      write windows-vm.desktop  -
prompts / confirm (exit)   marker already present    no marker
write_compose (exit)       marker already present    no marker
priv up fails (exit)       marker already present    no marker
priv up succeeds           -                         create_launcher_entry
```

The desktop entry content is unchanged. Re-running Install after a failed start reuses the existing mounts and overwrites the compose file, so that path recovers cleanly (source-traced, not executed).

### Setgid bit cleared when hardening storage directories

**Verified:** GNU `chmod 0700` keeps an existing set-group-ID bit on a directory (gnulib `mode_adjust` only clears it when the mode mentions it), leaving `2700`. That fails the exact-`700` checks in `prepare_caller_mounts` and `mounted_leaf_matches`. `a-s,u=rwx,go=` yields exactly `700`. Sandboxed runs of the real `prepare_user_mount_sources` from each revision, with a synthetic `$HOME`:

```text
$HOME mode        base .windows / Windows   head .windows / Windows
----------------  ------------------------  ------------------------
2755 (setgid)     2700 / 2700               700 / 700
755 (control)     700  / 700                700 / 700
```

The root-side chmod-and-check step was emulated as a non-root user with each revision's exact mode string (same `2700` vs `700` outcome); `prepare_caller_mounts` itself was not run as root.

**Verified:** the new `test/shell.d/windows-vm-launcher-test.sh` is picked up by `test/shell` and passes on the head. It fails against the base script and against two reordered variants (call moved before the prompts, and between the confirmation and `priv up`).

### Re-added `mkdir -p "$HOME/.windows"`

The fold adds `mkdir -p "$HOME/.windows"` after `omarchy-pkg-add` in `install_windows` ([head line 1189](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/9714bb9b85476f746d5944481f69415d48d5b175/bin/omarchy-windows-vm#L1189)). It arrives with #7985. Upstream commit c34d20ca removed this line when `prepare_user_mount_sources`, the first step of `install_windows`, took over creating and validating `~/.windows`.

**Impact:** none at runtime, since the directory always exists by that point. It is an unmentioned change unrelated to either commit's purpose.

**Suggested change:** drop the line.

**Optional test improvement:** nothing covers the setgid change. Setting `chmod 2755 "$HOME"` before calling `prepare_user_mount_sources` (for example in `windows-vm-compose-test.sh`, which already calls it) and asserting both directories end at `700` fails on the base (`2700`) and passes on the head, without privileges.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `bin/omarchy-windows-vm`, the menu entries that read `windows-vm.desktop`, the shell test runner, and GNU coreutils `chmod` / gnulib `modechange.c` (coreutils 9.7 and 9.12 sources). Sandboxed runs used coreutils 9.11 for `prepare_user_mount_sources` on base and head with synthetic setgid and plain home directories (identity lookup stubbed), and the new test on the head, against the base script and against two reordered variants. The full install, launch and remove flows (which need `/dev/kvm`, Docker and privileges) and the existing Windows VM compose and mount-boundary tests were not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
